## The packages

| Package | Path | What it owns |
|---|---|---|
| `@behaverse/studyflow-core` | `packages/core` | The headless document model: what a studyflow can contain, how it is read and written, how one element's attributes are reached. Depends only on `bpmn-moddle` and `js-yaml`. |
| the modeler | `packages/modeler` | The authoring app served at `app.html`: canvas, palette, inspector, templates, export, publishing. |
| the browser runner | `packages/runner` | The participant-facing app served at `./run/` — one folder per node kind under `src/nodes/`. |
| the CLI | `packages/cli` | The `studyflow` binary: `convert`, `validate`, `info`, `render`, `run`, all headless. It wires only the local runtime. |
| the Python runner | `packages/runner-py` | `studyflow_run.py`, which executes the analysis half of a studyflow by importing the Python each step names. |

| `core` folder, consumed by every other package | The question it answers |
|---|---|
| `notation/` | *What can a studyflow contain?* Parses `assets/schemas/*.moddle.yaml` into the queryable type catalog. |
| `document/` | *How is a studyflow read and written?* YAML ↔ BPMN 2.0 XML, PNG embedding, formatting, the two round-trip transforms. |
| `element/` | *What does this one element say?* Attribute access over a single moddle business object. |

### One folder per feature

Neither app has a `models/` / `views/` / `controllers/` split: a feature owns its whole stack, so `packages/modeler/src/palette/` holds the palette's data, its React, its bpmn-js registration, and its commands. Four file names recur.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `<feature>/commands.ts` | every bus command the feature handles |
| `<feature>/module.ts` | its bpmn-js registration, if it has one |
| `PascalCase.tsx` | one React view or one bpmn-js class, named after it |
| everything else | named for what it does |

## Two boundaries

Both are declared in `eslint.config.js`; inside a feature nothing further is policed.

| Boundary | What is banned | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/**` is framework-free | `react`, `react-dom`, `bpmn-js`, `diagram-js`, and both app aliases (`@modeler/*`, `@runner/*`) | `no-restricted-imports`, plus a `no-restricted-syntax` rule on service *names* |
| the modeler and the browser runner never import each other | `@runner/*` inside `packages/modeler/src/**`; `@modeler/*` inside `packages/runner/src/**` | `no-restricted-imports` |

The name rule catches what the import ban cannot: an identifier called `modeling`, `elementRegistry`, `commandStack`, `eventBus`, `injector`, `popupMenu`, `contextPad`, `bpmnFactory`, or `modeler` is an error anywhere under `packages/core/src/`, even when it arrives as an `any` parameter. Core takes data and returns data; the modeler passes in the bpmn-js adapter. Shared code therefore has exactly one place to go, and `packages/runner/package.json` lists React but not bpmn-js — its parser is `bpmn-moddle`.

## Who owns which pixels

The dividing line is the edge of the canvas: pixels inside the diagram's coordinate space are bpmn-js, which owns the SVG layer and the element lifecycle; everything outside is React.

| Surface | Owner | Where |
|---|---|---|
| nav bar, palette, inspector, settings dialog, notices | React | composed in `packages/modeler/src/app/App.tsx` |
| the canvas and shape rendering | bpmn-js | `packages/modeler/src/draw/` |
| context pad, append menu, colour swatches | bpmn-js | `packages/modeler/src/contextPad/` |
| label editing on the canvas | bpmn-js | `packages/modeler/src/bpmn/ChoreographyLabelEditing.ts`, which subclasses the stock provider and takes over its registration key |

Everything bpmn-js-side is registered in one list, `packages/modeler/src/bpmn/module.ts` — the first file to read for canvas behaviour. Because the palette sits outside the canvas, `packages/modeler/src/palette/module.ts` switches the stock one off with `paletteProvider: ['value', null]`.

## The command bus

A command's type *is* its handler's name. Dispatching `{ type: 'SetColor', elements, color }` runs `runSetColor`, exported from `packages/modeler/src/shape/commands.ts`: `executeCommand` searches the listed feature modules for an export called `run` followed by the command's type.

A feature joins the bus by appearing in the `FEATURES` array in `packages/modeler/src/commandBus.ts`, which is also where the types come from: the listed handlers' parameter types union into what may be dispatched — so a name nothing handles fails to compile — and a dispatch's result type is its handler's return type.

| Adding | What you edit |
|---|---|
| a command in an existing feature | export `run<Name>` from that feature's `commands.ts`, and dispatch `type: '<Name>'` |
| a command in a brand-new feature | the same, plus one line adding the module to `FEATURES` |

Both sides of the pixel split dispatch onto this bus, so `executeCommand`'s first parameter is typed `ServiceResolver | null`, not the modeler.

| A handler is handed | Which handlers, and why |
|---|---|
| anything with `get(name)` | Most of them. `runSetColor` is one line of `modeling`; `runInvalidateProvenanceRecord` reaches for `elementRegistry`, `moddle`, and `modeling` the same way. `packages/modeler/src/contextPad/ColorPickerProvider.ts` sends `{ type: 'SetColor' }` with `this.injector`, the bare didi injector bpmn-js hands its providers, because a popup-menu provider never sees the modeler. |
| the full modeler | Handlers that need the document rather than a service, and say so in their signature: `runPublishDiagram` and `runOpenRunner` call `saveXML`, exporting adds `saveSVG`, opening a diagram ends in `importXML`. |
| `null` | Boot. `packages/modeler/src/app/Modeler.tsx` dispatches `{ type: 'DownloadSchemas' }` and `{ type: 'CreateModeler' }` before there is a modeler to pass; their handlers declare `Modeler \| null` and ignore the argument, so startup is not a special path. |

`tests/commands.unit.spec.ts` collects the exported `run<Name>` handlers and scans the source tree for `type: '<Name>'` dispatches: a handler nothing dispatches fails, as does a command type with no handler.

## Schemas drive the modeler

Dropping a `*.moddle.yaml` file ([Authoring schemas](authoring-schemas.qmd)) into `assets/schemas/` is the whole registration step: `packages/core/src/notation/loader.ts` globs that directory at boot and compiles every file into the catalog, and no file names the new one. From it the modeler derives, with no code:

| Surface | What it is derived from |
|---|---|
| a palette entry and a drawn shape | any type that is neither abstract nor hidden; its palette group follows its own `meta.categories`, or its BPMN ancestor |
| an entry in the canvas append menu | the same types, read from the same catalog |
| inspector fields, filed under the inspector's tabs | the type's attributes and their `meta.categories` |
| a palette tile that drops in a ready-made fragment | a `templates` entry |
| round-tripping — attributes survive save and reload | the namespace `uri` |

::: {.callout-important title="Schema-driven stops at execution"}
A new type is drawable, inspectable, and round-trippable the moment its schema loads, but it is not yet *runnable*. The browser runner matches each flow node to a definition registered under `packages/runner/src/nodes/<kind>/`; where nothing matches, `packages/runner/src/nodes/index.ts` warns that the type is not executable and the run steps past it. Writing that node module is what makes a type execute ([Add a node kind to the browser runner](runner-nodes.qmd)).
:::

## What an export sees

`packages/modeler/src/export/model.ts` walks the element registry once, in registry order, resolving each element against the catalog: the roles of both its BPMN host type and the schema type it wraps, every declared attribute carrying a value, and — for a data operation — the ids it reads and writes, all flattened to plain data. `packages/modeler/src/export/commands.ts` builds it on demand.

| Exporter | Its input | The rule |
|---|---|---|
| `linkml.ts`, `nidm.ts`, `artemis.ts` | that one walk | Each is a pure `ExportModel -> string`: no bpmn-js, no moddle, no walk of its own. It may put a question to the catalog directly, as LinkML does for attribute ranges, but it may not go back to the canvas. |
| `drawio.ts` | the modeler | It projects geometry and diagram interchange — positions, waypoints, colours, mxGraph styles — which the model does not carry. Meaning and geometry are two different exports. |

Widen `buildExportModel` and the LinkML, NIDM, and ARTEM-IS exports widen together. `tests/export-conformance.unit.spec.ts` runs all three over every diagram in `assets/examples/`, so a change to what the model collects has to hold across everything we ship.

## Where the provenance lanes come from

The Provenance view draws `git log --graph` lanes from the document alone: `packages/modeler/src/provenance/records.ts` reads the study's own trail plus the `prov:Activity` entries on individual elements, and opens no repository to do it. [Views and the record](../run/provenance.qmd) explains what those entries mean.

The graph turns on one derived flag. `collectProvenance` marks an `invalidated` marker **consumed** once the record it names — by `what`, which holds that record's `when` — no longer stands, superseded or replaced by a later run. A marker still standing gets `pendingBranch`, the dashed stub the view draws in place of a lane. From each consumed marker, `assignLanes` works out three things.

| What it looks for | How it finds it |
|---|---|
| the run that branched | the *first* executed record to supersede the marker's named one — not the latest, or two branches that re-ran the same step collapse into one lane — and the document-level `executed` stamp that record falls under |
| where the lane is | the lane counter advances at that stamp's row, so the stamp and every row below it sit one lane to the right |
| where its line starts | at the consumed marker's row rather than the stamp's: that row carries `opens`, the curve leaves its dot, and the new lane's straight line picks up on the row below |

`displayOrder` moves each precise marker (one carrying a `what`) to sit immediately after the executed record it names, and that is the whole of its job: `collectProvenance` returns records strictly oldest-first, and a ✕ is stamped long after the run it voids, so in time order the branch would open nowhere near its target. It is display-only in two senses — the view is its only caller, and it splices the array it is handed, so `Provenance.tsx` passes the copy its filter has already made rather than the memoised collection every other consumer reads.

`tests/provenance-view.unit.spec.ts` pins both halves of the branch rule: the lane opens at the consumed marker's row rather than at the run stamp, and one step re-run under two later runs still opens two separate lanes.

## Running it locally

The CLI builds to one self-contained file, which the top-level build does not cover.

```bash
npm run dev                                    # modeler on :5173, browser runner proxied at /run
npm run build -w @behaverse/studyflow-cli      # the CLI, built once
node packages/cli/dist/studyflow.mjs --help    # then run it from anywhere in the repo
```

| Script | Runs |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Both dev servers on one address: the modeler on `:5173`, passing `/run` to the browser runner on `:5174`. |
| `npm run build` | Production builds of the modeler and the browser runner. |
| `npm run docs` | A preview of the documentation, without opening a browser. |
| `npm run examples:render` | Builds the CLI, then re-draws every example image with `studyflow render`. |

: The scripts that are not tests or guards; those are below. {#tbl-scripts}

## Where the tests live

Every test is in `tests/` at the repo root, and Playwright runs them in two lanes.

| Lane | Config | Matches | Needs a browser |
|---|---|---|---|
| unit (`npm run test:unit`) | `playwright.unit.config.ts` | `tests/**/*.unit.spec.ts` | no — no dev server, no DOM |
| e2e (`npm run test:e2e`) | the `e2e` project in `playwright.config.ts` | everything else in `tests/` | yes, plus two dev servers |

The fast lane is browserless because `core` is framework-free: a unit spec reads the shipped schemas off disk through `tests/schemas.ts`, the Node counterpart of the loader's bundler glob. The e2e project boots the modeler on `127.0.0.1:4173` and the browser runner on `4174`, with the modeler proxying `/run` so both sit on one origin, as the merged build is served.

| Guard | What it holds to |
|---|---|
| `npm run lint` | the two boundaries above |
| `npm run lint:schemas` | the shipped schemas parse, compile, and stay well-formed |
| `npm run lint:docs` | every element name a page prints resolves to one some shipped schema declares, retired names stay retired, every relative link resolves *and* stays inside `docs/`, every page declares a title and a description |
| `npm run typecheck` | the command bus's name check, which is only real where `tsc` runs; CI runs it on every push |
